title: SLO Orchestra Conductor - 90 Day Roadmap
content:
Purpose:
This is a working 90-day plan for the cross-functional reliability program focused on SLO adoption, testable rollouts, and operationalizing observable controls across hosted and dedicated inference paths. Framing: think of the program as an orchestra — each team is an instrument. The Conductor role (program lead) coordinates rehearsals (sprints), scores (runbooks/SLIs), and the public performance (SLO-backed launches).

High-level objectives (90 days):
- Define and validate SLIs for critical customer-flows (inference API, streaming, embeddings) with measurable signal and low-noise baselines.
- Deliver SLO contracts for 3 canonical services and run two canary rollouts with rollback criteria.
- Implement per-route latency percentile instrumentation (p50/p95/p99) and token-cost telemetry in Console dashboards.
- Ship automated alert-to-incident mappings and one-click fallback playbooks for degraded model variants.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Hosted API and Dedicated share telemetry pipelines; Private deployments are out-of-scope for the first 90 days except for requirements capture.
- Core KPI owners: Product will approve SLO targets; Eng-SRE will own alerting and runbooks; Serving Runtime will implement tracing hooks and prefix/KV cache metrics.
- Capacity: two engineers allocated full-time from eng-sre, one from serving-runtime, product manager 0.2 FTE.

Roles & responsibilities (quick):
- Conductor / Program Lead: Aisha Patel — orchestration, stakeholder updates, rolling decisions.
- Score Authors (SLI/SLO definitions): Miles Chen (eng-sre), Sofia Gomez (serving-runtime).
- Diagnostics & Dashboards: Rahul Kapoor (observability) + Console PM.
- Runbook / Playbook Owner: Oncall Lead + Reliability Docs steward.
- Rollout Eng: feature teams owning each customer flow.

90-day sprint sequence (12 weeks broken into 3 four-week cycles):
Cycle 0: Prep & discovery (weeks 1-2, partial week 3)
- Inventory candidate services and customer-flows (API text-gen, chat streaming, embeddings).
- Quick fidelity check: validate 30-day telemetry availability per flow.
- Stakeholder alignment workshop: finalize SLO consumer groups and criticalness matrix.
- Deliverable: SLO candidate spreadsheet + prioritized service list.

Cycle 1: Define & instrument (weeks 3-6)
- Produce SLI definitions (latency percentiles, error-rate semantics, successful-response tokens).
- Implement instrumentation changes (tracing hooks, token counters) in serving-runtime — target merge windows: weeks 4-5.
- Create Console dashboards for per-route SLI visualization.
- Run synthetic experiments (traffic-replay) to surface noise and adjust SLI boundaries.
- Deliverable: 3 authored SLO contracts (draft), instrumentation PRs, dashboard prototypes.

Cycle 2: Test & rollout (weeks 7-10)
- Canary plan for service A (text generation): small percentage in staging then production.
- Validate alert thresholds and incident runbooks in a staged incident drill (tabletop + simulated metric shift).
- Create automatic fallback automation (route to cheaper model-variant, degrade to cached responses) and test during canary.
- Gather quality metrics and product-signoff for SLO targets.
- Deliverable: Canary report, updated runbooks, rollback playbook.

Cycle 3: Harden & handoff (weeks 11-12)
- Finalize SLO acceptance criteria and gate for team-level adoption templates.
- Prepare onboarding kit and short training: "SLO conductor kit" (slide deck, checklist, runbook template).
- Handoff to steady-state reliability guild + calendar of quarterly reviews.
- Deliverable: Handoff package, backlog of follow-ups, post-mortem of canary lessons.

Acceptance criteria for an SLO to be considered "adopted":
- SLIs are backed by >=30 days of representative telemetry and have documented noise characteristics.
- Dashboards showing p50/p95/p99 and error-rate for route-level slices exist and update within 2 minutes of ingestion.
- There is a tested alert-to-incident mapping that produces a playbook with runbook steps and an incident commander assignment.
- Canary metrics are within agreed rollback thresholds OR a rollback has been executed and documented.

Operational runbooks (template highlights):
- Triggering conditions: exact metric expressions (e.g., p95_latency(route=X) > 2s for 5m).
- Triage steps: quick checks (upstream fail, model-variant health, cache thrashing, infra saturation).
- Automated mitigation: route-fallback, model-variant downgrade, traffic-shedding percentages.
- Post-incident actions: signal changes, SLI adjustments, ticket to product to consider SLO change.

Communication cadence / stakeholder rituals:
- Weekly Conductor sync (30m) — cross-functional alignment, blockers, decisions required.
- Bi-weekly Rehearsal (60m) — hands-on review of dashboards and ongoing canary metrics with engineers.
- Monthly Exec snapshot — high-level SLO adoption progress and customer-impact summary.
- Incident retro loop: standard 7-day and 30-day follow-throughs.

Risks and open questions (notes to self):
- Risk: metric cardinality explosion when exposing route-level SLIs across 200+ routes. Mitigation: sampling, pre-aggregation, and a canonical route taxonomy.
- Open: how to account for variable prompt length when defining latency SLOs that are per-request vs per-token. TODO: propose dual-metric approach (per-request latency for tail; per-token throughput for cost-aware triggers).
- Risk: product pushback on strict SLOs that could increase infrastructure cost. Mitigation: include cost window analysis and conservative initial SLOs with gradual tightening.

Checklist (near-term action items):
- [ ] Finalize SLO consumer map and priority list by Mar 1.
- [ ] Merge instrumentation PRs for text-gen and embeddings by Mar 15.
- [ ] Kickoff canary for text-gen service by Apr 1.
- [ ] Run tabletop incident drill week of Apr 5.
- [ ] Draft SLO acceptance guide and onboarding kit by Apr 12.

Short example: SLO contract (draft) for "Text Generation - Hosted API":
- SLI: successful-response latency p95 (request end-to-end) measured over 5m windows; exclude cold-starts during deploy windows.
- SLO target: 99.5% of requests p95 < 1.8s (initial conservative target).
- Error budget: 0.5% per 30-day window; automated alert at 50% burn rate sustained for 30m.
- Rollout gating: fail canary if p95 exceeds 3s or error-rate > 0.8% for 5m.

Artifacts to produce (by owner):
- SLO contracts (Google Sheet canonical): Miles Chen.
- Instrumentation PRs: Sofia Gomez + runtime engineers.
- Console dashboard pack: Rahul Kapoor + Console PM.
- Runbook templates and automation scripts: Oncall lead + Eng-SRE docs.

Appendix / notes:
- Quick links: Confluence SLO library (see linked_artifacts), existing reliability infra tickets (ENG-4721, ENG-4983).
- Slack channels: #reliability-cadence for daily updates; #infra-deploys for rollout windows.
- Thought: consider an "SLO explorer" internal tool to map services -> SLIs -> owners; low priority but high value for longer-term governance.

Unresolved heuristics (capture for next workshop):
- Should SLOs be request-count-weighted or revenue-weighted? (Product question)
- How to handle multi-tenant privacy of metrics when surfacing route-level dashboards across shared accounts?

----
Versioning notes: this is a working draft. Next steps: review with Product and Serving Runtime team on 2026-03-12, incorporate instrumentation timeline, then move to in_review.

-- Aisha (Conductor)
